Re: Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Reference number: POC-F4C641ED8B-99591  
Requested service: Lumbar decompression/discectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Date of denial notice: August 23, 2026

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar decompression/discectomy. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request that Ambetter overturn the denial and authorize the procedure.

I am an adult patient with a documented herniated lumbar disc. The clinical records establish the following:

- I have had 24 months of progressive lower-back pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, from April 24, 2026, through July 17, 2026, for a total of 18 visits. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 17, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- MRI of the lumbar spine on June 26, 2026, showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral-recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain extending into the right calf.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use condition. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.
- The requested procedure was prescribed by Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery.

These records demonstrate a persistent, function-limiting condition with objective imaging findings, nerve-root compression, corresponding neurologic findings, and failure of extensive nonsurgical treatment. The MRI findings at L4-L5 correspond to the right-sided radicular symptoms and neurologic deficit. The requested decompression is directed at the documented nerve-root compression rather than nonspecific back pain alone.

The publicly available policy information previously identified includes adult age and diagnosis of a herniated lumbar disc among the requirements for open discectomy or microdiscectomy. My date of birth and age are [date of birth/age]. The submitted records establish the herniated lumbar disc and the associated objective compression and neurologic impairment.

I am not quoting the plan’s full policy because the full policy text was not retrievable in the materials reviewed. Please provide, as part of this appeal, the complete medical-necessity criteria and policy version used for this determination, identify each criterion that Ambetter believes was not met, and provide the clinical rationale for the denial. If InterQual criteria or delegated-vendor criteria were used, please provide those criteria and the specific findings relied upon.

Please review the enclosed clinical records, including the MRI report, physical-therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s request. Based on the documented diagnosis, objective nerve-root compression, neurologic deficit, functional impairment, and failed conservative care, I request authorization for CPT 63030.

Please send the appeal determination in writing. This appeal must be received by February 19, 2027.

Sincerely,

Morgan Foster  
Member ID: W162894592
